profiles.summary: A start-to-present account of Tyler's path from Odd Future's self-published world through a sequence of increasingly distinct album eras.
profiles.tagline: From teenage collective architect to album-world builder.

chapters.title: The collective is the first canvas
chapters.dek: Tyler helped assemble Odd Future around music, artwork, video, clothing, and a direct online relationship with listeners. Bastard made his own voice the entrance to that larger homemade world.

chapters.title: Provocation opens into arrangement
chapters.dek: Goblin carried the breakout intensity of the early period, while Wolf and Cherry Bomb widened Tyler's palette through character writing, live instrumentation, dense harmony, and more ambitious sequencing.

chapters.title: Flower Boy brings the interior forward
chapters.dek: Contemporary critics described Flower Boy as a more concise and introspective turn. That is a critical reading of the record—not a diagnosis of Tyler's private life.

song_links.label: Read and hear the turning point

chapters.title: IGOR turns an emotional arc into a full album world
chapters.dek: IGOR joined writing, production, visual identity, and sequencing into one tightly controlled narrative project; the Recording Academy later recognized it with the rap-album Grammy.

chapters.title: CALL ME IF YOU GET LOST makes motion part of the story
chapters.dek: The album used the Tyler Baudelaire persona, travel imagery, and mixtape narration to stage confidence and complication; The Estate Sale later expanded that chapter with songs from the same sessions.

chapters.title: CHROMAKOPIA tests control against responsibility
chapters.dek: The Recording Academy's album analysis places CHROMAKOPIA after Tyler's earlier breakthroughs and emphasizes its recurring questions about self-control, adulthood, family, and the stories people construct around him.

chapters.title: DON'T TAP THE GLASS ends the current album line in motion
chapters.dek: The current reviewed catalog closes with the compact 2025 album DON'T TAP THE GLASS. Its release extends the pattern of treating each album as a distinct musical and visual environment rather than a sequel to the last one.

profiles.summary: The complete local spine of Odd Future: friends publishing their own world, a sudden public breakthrough, and a network of individual careers and subgroups.
profiles.tagline: One collective, many finished and continuing paths.

chapters.title: Friends build the platform they need
chapters.dek: Odd Future began as a Los Angeles network of teenage rappers, producers, skaters, photographers, and friends. Early tapes established a shared banner without requiring every member to sound alike.

chapters.title: Free releases make the site a destination
chapters.dek: Members posted mixtapes, videos, images, and everyday footage directly to the internet. Radical captures the collective's competitive, crowded energy before the wider industry arrived.

chapters.title: Visibility arrives without surrendering the umbrella
chapters.dek: Television appearances, volatile live shows, and press attention accelerated the group's rise. Its 2011 label arrangement was reported as preserving an Odd Future imprint and unusual creative control.

chapters.title: Oldie becomes the ensemble portrait
chapters.dek: The OF Tape Vol. 2 gathered multiple voices under one release. Oldie works as the clearest musical doorway into the roster because its long relay makes difference inside the group audible.

chapters.title: The group recedes; the network remains visible
chapters.dek: Odd Future stopped operating like a conventional active rap group, while Tyler, Frank, Earl, Syd, The Internet, Domo, Mike G, the production teams, and the screen performers continued along distinct paths. The archive treats those branches as the ending, not as evidence that every relationship stayed the same.

profiles.summary: From songwriter and Odd Future member to the authored album worlds of channel ORANGE, Endless, and Blonde.
profiles.tagline: A quiet branch whose albums changed the scale of the whole map.

chapters.title: A songwriter steps forward under his own name
chapters.dek: After writing for other performers, Frank Ocean joined Odd Future's wider circle and released nostalgia,ULTRA. The mixtape made his narrative writing and unusual source material the center of attention.

chapters.title: channel ORANGE expands the frame
chapters.dek: channel ORANGE turned linked character studies, social detail, and warm, flexible production into a major-label album. The Recording Academy recognized it with the Grammy for urban contemporary album.

chapters.title: Two releases separate process from final statement
chapters.dek: The visual album Endless arrived first, followed one day later by Blonde. Together they marked a new independent phase and a looser, more fragmented way of arranging memory, voice, and time.

chapters.title: Blonde remains the current full-album endpoint
chapters.dek: This archive does not turn gaps between albums into a private-life story. It ends Frank Ocean's album line at Blonde while preserving later work as a subject for future sourced updates.

song_links.label: Return to the current album endpoint

profiles.summary: Syd's path from teenage engineer and Odd Future DJ to The Internet's lead voice, solo artist, and the 2026 album Beard.
profiles.tagline: The engineer behind the room becomes the voice at its center.

chapters.title: The guesthouse studio becomes infrastructure
chapters.dek: Syd said she built a studio in her parents' guesthouse as a teenager and initially wanted to produce and sing hooks. That room became part of Odd Future's practical recording environment.

chapters.title: A separate band grows from the same network
chapters.dek: Syd and Matt Martians formed The Internet in 2011. Purple Naked Ladies and Feel Good moved toward a band language distinct from Odd Future's rap releases.

chapters.title: Ego Death makes the band visible on its own terms
chapters.dek: By Ego Death, The Internet's fuller lineup and live-band chemistry had become the central story. Syd's restrained vocal presence anchored songs built from space, rhythm, and ensemble interplay.

chapters.title: Solo records bring the voice closer
chapters.dek: Fin established Syd's solo catalog beside the band rather than erasing it. Broken Hearts Club continued that line with a more intimate, relationship-centered album frame.

chapters.title: Beard arrives as The Internet reconvenes
chapters.dek: Syd released her third solo album Beard in 2026 and publicly discussed returning to work with The Internet. The two paths now continue alongside each other.

profiles.summary: The band's full released arc—from Syd and Matt Martians' home-studio partnership through Ego Death, Hive Mind, solo branches, and the announced next chapter.
profiles.tagline: A side project becomes a durable band, then learns how to reunite.

chapters.title: A living room becomes the first band room
chapters.dek: Syd and Matt Martians said they met online, became roommates, and worked in a living-room studio. Purple Naked Ladies records the moment their collaboration became The Internet.

chapters.title: Feel Good widens the lineup and the sound
chapters.dek: Feel Good moved the project toward richer live instrumentation and the ensemble format that would define its next phase.

chapters.title: Ego Death turns chemistry into a breakthrough
chapters.dek: Ego Death sharpened the exchange among Syd, Matt Martians, Patrick Paige II, Christopher Smith, and then-new guitarist Steve Lacy. Its Grammy nomination gave the band an identity legible beyond the Odd Future connection.

chapters.title: Solo branches feed back into Hive Mind
chapters.dek: The members released individual projects, then returned with new experience. In interviews around Hive Mind, they described those solo paths as strengthening rather than ending the band.

chapters.title: A long pause becomes an announced next chapter
chapters.dek: In July 2026, the band said it had worked on and off for years and was aiming to release a new album in early 2027. Because that record is not released, this story ends with the announcement—not a prediction about its sound.

profiles.summary: An early Odd Future contributor whose producer-rapper identity continued through an independent catalog of his own.
profiles.tagline: An early branch with a production language beyond the collective.

chapters.title: Production links the first Odd Future orbit
chapters.dek: brandUn DeShay contributed during Odd Future's early formation and worked in the Super D3Shay configuration connected to Matt Martians' production world.

chapters.title: The producer-rapper identity moves outside the group
chapters.dek: In his 2011 interview, DeShay discussed building his own work after the Odd Future period and treating rapping and production as parts of one career.

chapters.title: goldUn Child: 2 closes the indexed album line
chapters.dek: The synchronized release catalog currently ends at goldUn Child: 2. Threadline records that endpoint without inventing a story for undocumented gaps after it.

profiles.summary: A teenage Odd Future co-founder who chose an independent solo vision and built the Peas & Carrots path around it.
profiles.tagline: From the first tape to a deliberately separate Los Angeles career.

related.relationship: Early Odd Future peer and later collaborator

chapters.title: Two beginnings happen at once
chapters.dek: Casey Veggies helped form Odd Future while also releasing Customized Greatly, Volume 1 as a teenager. His own catalog therefore starts beside the collective, not after it.

chapters.title: A different vision becomes Peas & Carrots
chapters.dek: Veggies described building a separate rap path and the Peas & Carrots label-and-clothing identity. Live & Grow brought that long mixtape apprenticeship into a studio-album frame.

chapters.title: The independent catalog keeps extending
chapters.dek: The local catalog documents a sustained run of Customized Greatly sequels, collaborative tapes, and independent releases through Caught Up In The Game: Deluxe Edition in 2026.

profiles.summary: Domo Genesis moves from Odd Future's early mixtape exchange into a patient solo catalog shaped by collaboration and reflection.
profiles.tagline: The collective's grounded rapper builds a long solo line.

related.relationship: Member with Hodgy and Left Brain

chapters.title: Rolling Papers introduces a steadier voice
chapters.dek: Domo Genesis entered Odd Future's free-mixtape period with Rolling Papers, establishing a relaxed but technically focused presence inside the louder collective frame.

chapters.title: Collaboration becomes the route outward
chapters.dek: No Idols with The Alchemist and the MellowHigh album connected Domo's Odd Future role to producer-led work beyond the main group tapes.

chapters.title: Genesis makes the solo album personal
chapters.dek: Domo described Genesis as a full debut shaped by experience outside the collective's early rush, with family, ambition, and self-assessment moving closer to the center.

chapters.title: Later records keep the story in motion
chapters.dek: Intros, Outros & Interludes foregrounded reflection, and the synchronized catalog continues through SCRAM! in 2025. The through-line is documented output, not a claim that the music remained stylistically fixed.

profiles.summary: From the startling teenage Earl tape to an increasingly compressed, collaborative, and self-directed album language.
profiles.tagline: A prodigy story becomes a long study in authorship and scale.

chapters.title: The Earl tape makes a teenage voice impossible to ignore
chapters.dek: Earl's first tape paired dense internal rhyme with the abrasive imagination of Odd Future's early web era. Its notoriety made his absence from the group's breakthrough part of the public story around him.

chapters.title: Doris turns a return into a debut album
chapters.dek: After returning to Los Angeles, Earl released Doris: still connected to Odd Future, but already organized around his own pacing, collaborators, and unease with easy narratives.

chapters.title: The music contracts around voice and pressure
chapters.dek: I Don't Like Shit, I Don't Go Outside reduced the scale and darkened the production, making brevity and interior detail central to Earl's album craft.

chapters.title: Fragments become a new compositional language
chapters.dek: Some Rap Songs and the records that followed used short forms, looped textures, and close collaboration to move further from conventional rap-album structure. Earl later framed growth as more important than recreating the old collective era.

song_links.label: Hear the Some Rap Songs coda

chapters.title: The catalog remains collaborative and active
chapters.dek: The synchronized catalog continues beyond Voir Dire through POMPEII // UTILITY in 2026. Threadline treats those release records as the current endpoint and leaves interpretation to reviewed sources as they arrive.

profiles.summary: A founding rapper whose story runs through MellowHype, the collective tapes, and a solo catalog that eventually carries his own name.
profiles.tagline: From Odd Future's first exchanges to a separate solo voice.

related.relationship: Member with Domo Genesis and Left Brain

chapters.title: A founding voice develops inside a duo
chapters.dek: Hodgy was present in Odd Future's earliest formation while his work with Left Brain as MellowHype created a durable rapper-producer unit inside the group.

chapters.title: Solo tapes sit beside the group work
chapters.dek: The Dena Tape and later EPs documented a separate Hodgy catalog even as he remained one of the most frequent voices on Odd Future and MellowHype releases.

chapters.title: Trio, duo, and solo formats overlap
chapters.dek: MellowHigh placed Hodgy beside Domo and Left Brain; INSA continued MellowHype; Fireplace: TheNotTheOtherSide then established a full solo-album chapter.

chapters.title: Entitled closes the current indexed line
chapters.dek: Released under the shorter name Hodgy, Entitled is the latest album-length project in the synchronized catalog and marks the current endpoint of this reviewed chronology.

profiles.summary: Tyler and Jasper's brief comedy-rap duo, preserved as one of the earliest recorded artifacts in the Odd Future family tree.
profiles.tagline: A six-song teenage experiment that points toward the larger collective.

chapters.title: Tyler and Jasper make a duo out of friendship
chapters.dek: I Smell Panties paired Tyler's early production with Jasper's comic performance before either career had settled into a public shape.

chapters.title: One self-released EP becomes the whole catalog
chapters.dek: The official Odd Future Bandcamp page dates the six-track I Smell Panties release to June 28, 2008. Its small scale is the story: a complete early experiment, not an unfinished album series.

song_links.label: Hear the middle of the EP

chapters.title: Lisa bridges the duo into Odd Future's first tape
chapters.dek: Lisa appears in both the duo's compact catalog and The Odd Future Tape, making it the clearest connection between this side project and the collective's first shared release.

profiles.summary: A founding friend whose importance to Odd Future runs through comic performance, group records, Loiter Squad, and an enduring on-screen presence.
profiles.tagline: The story is performance and friendship, not a missing solo album.

related.relationship: Odd Future and Loiter Squad castmate
Odd Future and Loiter Squad castmate

chapters.title: Friendship is the role before music is the product
chapters.dek: Jasper was part of Odd Future's founding social world and formed I Smell Panties with Tyler. The duo's comic records show why a solo discography is the wrong measure of his contribution.

chapters.title: The nontraditional rapper becomes essential on screen
chapters.dek: Jasper's appearances on Tyler and Odd Future records were inseparable from videos, stage energy, and group chemistry; Oldie's ensemble video preserves that role clearly.

chapters.title: Loiter Squad makes performance the main medium
chapters.dek: Adult Swim's Loiter Squad moved Jasper, Taco, L-Boy, Tyler, and their peers into sketch and stunt television, formalizing the comedy already present in the collective's videos.

chapters.title: The public path stays on screen and inside the extended family
chapters.dek: Jasper continued through reality, film, and television work and remained visible around Camp Flog Gnaw. The New Yorker's 2024 profile treats that continuing presence as its own career, not a footnote to music.

profiles.summary: The producer at the center of MellowHype and MellowHigh, followed into the independent Mind Gone and LEFT FAMOUS catalogs.
profiles.tagline: A production backbone becomes a solo catalog.

chapters.title: MellowHype gives Odd Future a producer-rapper engine
chapters.dek: Left Brain's production partnership with Hodgy began in Odd Future's founding period and developed into MellowHype's own run of releases.

chapters.title: MellowHigh widens the unit
chapters.dek: Adding Domo Genesis to Hodgy and Left Brain created MellowHigh, a trio whose sole album emphasized the producer's role as connective tissue between rappers.

chapters.title: Mind Gone moves the producer name to the cover
chapters.dek: Left Brain described Mind Gone as an ongoing independent project connected to his Odd Future history but organized under his own name and collaborators.

chapters.title: LEFT FAMOUS extends the independent line
chapters.dek: The synchronized catalog currently ends with LEFT FAMOUS in 2025, documenting that Left Brain's released work continued beyond the original group and subgroup cycles.

profiles.summary: Lionel Boyce's route from Odd Future friend and Loiter Squad performer to an acting career led by The Bear.
profiles.tagline: A collective role grows into a screen career under his own name.
profiles.coverage: Reviewed story · early Odd Future–present screen work

Odd Future and Loiter Squad castmate

chapters.title: L-Boy is part of the social architecture
chapters.dek: Lionel Boyce entered the public Odd Future story as L-Boy, one of the friends whose humor and presence helped define the collective beyond records.

chapters.title: Loiter Squad becomes an informal acting school
chapters.dek: Boyce performed in the Adult Swim series with Tyler, Jasper, and Taco. The show translated the group's homemade video humor into recurring television production.

chapters.title: Lionel Boyce becomes the credited identity
chapters.dek: Boyce's later acting work, especially Marcus on The Bear, established a career legible beyond the L-Boy nickname. His conversations with Travis Bennett place that growth on a continuous line from their Odd Future beginnings.

song_links.label: Return to where the screen path began

profiles.summary: A producer's line through the Super 3, The Jet Age of Tomorrow, Odd Future, The Internet, and a parallel solo catalog.
profiles.tagline: The connective producer behind several branches of the family tree.

chapters.title: Internet beat-making leads into Odd Future
chapters.dek: Matt Martians published beats online under the Super 3 idea before connecting with Tyler and the early Odd Future network. The Super D3Shay configuration records that first production branch.

chapters.title: The Jet Age of Tomorrow builds the instrumental branch
chapters.dek: With Pyramid Vritra, Martians developed a science-fiction-leaning production catalog that ran beside Odd Future's rap tapes and prepared the collaborative habits of his next band.

chapters.title: The producer becomes a band architect
chapters.dek: Martians formed The Internet with Syd and helped turn a home-studio partnership into a working band whose first major breakthrough was Ego Death.

chapters.title: Solo albums extend the production vocabulary
chapters.dek: The Drum Chord Theory opened Martians' solo line, which continued alongside The Internet. He later described that solo work as an extension of ideas developed in Jet Age rather than a rejection of them.

song_links.track_title: Spend the Night / If You Were My GF
song_links.label: Enter the solo catalog

chapters.title: The band connection becomes active again
chapters.dek: The Internet's 2026 update places Martians back inside an active band process aimed at a 2027 album. The archive records the announced work without claiming to know its unfinished form.

song_links.label: Return to the last band chapter

profiles.summary: The one-album trio formed by Hodgy, Domo Genesis, and Left Brain at the height of Odd Future's subgroup era.
profiles.tagline: Three familiar roles recombined for one compact chapter.

chapters.title: MellowHype adds Domo Genesis
chapters.dek: MellowHigh combined Hodgy and Left Brain's existing duo with Domo Genesis, creating a subgroup that could reuse established chemistry in a new three-person balance.

chapters.title: A documentary trail follows the self-titled album
chapters.dek: The FADER's Odd World episode documented the trio recording and touring around MellowHigh, giving the subgroup a public story beyond a name in the roster.

chapters.title: The trio ends as a one-album branch
chapters.dek: The synchronized catalog contains one MellowHigh album. Hodgy, Domo Genesis, and Left Brain continued through solo and other subgroup work, so their individual pages carry the story forward.

profiles.summary: Hodgy and Left Brain's foundational rapper-producer duo, from early tapes through Numbers, INSA, and a later reunion.
profiles.tagline: The durable duo inside Odd Future's first wave.

chapters.title: A rapper-producer pairing forms inside the collective
chapters.dek: Hodgy and Left Brain established MellowHype during Odd Future's founding years. YelloWhite and BlackenedWhite gave the early roster a complete subgroup catalog beside Tyler's releases.

chapters.title: The duo reaches its formal album phase
chapters.dek: After the free-mixtape period, Numbers placed MellowHype inside Odd Future Records' commercial release cycle while preserving Left Brain's production and Hodgy's voice as the core unit.

chapters.title: INSA closes the main run
chapters.dek: INSA followed the duo's earlier releases, after which Hodgy said MellowHype would stop operating as an album project even though the two musicians could still work together.

chapters.title: A reunion changes the period, not the history
chapters.dek: The duo reunited publicly for Tisk in 2017. That return is best read as a later connection between Hodgy and Left Brain, not proof that the original Odd Future structure resumed.

song_links.label: Return to the defining duo sound

profiles.summary: A low-key rapper and DJ whose Odd Future role became a steady independent mixtape and album catalog.
profiles.tagline: A quieter counterweight with one of the roster's longest catalogs.

chapters.title: Mike G enters with a contrasting cadence
chapters.dek: Mike G joined the early Odd Future circle and brought a lower-key delivery that widened the collective's range rather than copying its most visible voices.

chapters.title: ALI establishes the solo entry point
chapters.dek: The ALI project arrived during the group's free-release surge and remains the clearest early doorway into Mike G apart from ensemble appearances.

chapters.title: Group verses and DJ work run together
chapters.dek: Mike G remained audible on group releases while developing a DJ practice. Forest Green, included in the collective catalog, is a direct bridge between the solo voice and the Odd Future banner.

song_links.label: Hear the bridge to the group

chapters.title: The catalog continues outside the group cycle
chapters.dek: Mike G's synchronized catalog extends through Verses, Exile, and Aliteia. The sequence documents continuity after Odd Future ceased acting like a conventional group.

profiles.summary: A skater, performer, and rapper whose Odd Future connection opens into film work and a growing solo music catalog.
profiles.tagline: Skating, screen performance, and music share one creative path.

chapters.title: Skating is the entrance to the extended collective
chapters.dek: Na-Kel Smith came through the Los Angeles skate world around Odd Future. His presence shows how the collective's boundary included physical culture, video, and friendship as well as formal membership credits.

chapters.title: mid90s turns lived skate knowledge into screen work
chapters.dek: Smith's performance in Jonah Hill's mid90s brought his skate background into a major film role. Interviews from the release period connect that acting work to the same community that shaped his music.

song_links.label: Follow the energy into his music

chapters.title: The solo catalog becomes a primary lane
chapters.dek: 3000nakteen and the releases that followed established Smith as a recording artist in his own right, not only a guest in someone else's story.

chapters.title: NAK extends the music line
chapters.dek: The synchronized catalog currently ends with NAK in 2026. Threadline records that release as the present endpoint while keeping film, skating, and music visible as parallel parts of the story.

profiles.summary: Pyramid Vritra's route from teenage production with Matt Martians to The Jet Age of Tomorrow and an extensive experimental solo catalog as Vritra.
profiles.tagline: The Jet Age launches a long independent production journey.

chapters.title: A teenage collaboration becomes the Jet Age
chapters.dek: Vritra described connecting with Matt Martians as a teenager and making music together inside Odd Future's wider production world. The partnership became The Jet Age of Tomorrow.

chapters.title: Solo releases begin beside the duo
chapters.dek: Elouise and Pyramid established a solo line while Jet Age albums were still arriving. The parallel catalogs show that the duo and the individual producer were never mutually exclusive identities.

chapters.title: Vritra becomes the durable working name
chapters.dek: The later catalog shortens the name and ranges through numerous producer-led albums. In interview, Vritra framed the work through experimentation and long-term collaboration rather than nostalgia for one collective era.

chapters.title: AMBER closes the current indexed line
chapters.dek: With one of the largest catalogs in this archive, Vritra's story currently reaches AMBER in 2024. The release count makes the solo branch a major body of work, not a subgroup footnote.

profiles.summary: Travis Bennett's path from teenage Odd Future DJ and hypeman through Loiter Squad into a sustained television and film career.
profiles.tagline: The DJ booth opens into acting under his own name.
profiles.coverage: Reviewed story · teenage Odd Future–present screen work

related.relationship: Odd Future and Loiter Squad castmate
Odd Future and Loiter Squad castmate

chapters.title: Taco grows up in public as the group's DJ
chapters.dek: Travis Bennett entered Odd Future as a teenager, performing as Taco and serving as Tyler's DJ and hypeman while the collective moved from local shows to international attention.

chapters.title: Loiter Squad makes the camera a second stage
chapters.dek: Bennett joined Tyler, Jasper, L-Boy, and other members in the Adult Swim sketch series, learning screen performance inside the collective's existing comic language.

chapters.title: Acting becomes a choice, not a side effect
chapters.dek: Bennett has explained that he did not want the expected next step of making his own rap career. He pursued acting instead, eventually becoming Elz on Dave.

chapters.title: Travis Bennett becomes the durable public identity
chapters.dek: Later interviews with Bennett and Lionel Boyce frame their screen careers as growth from the same friendships, while making clear that each now works under an identity larger than an Odd Future nickname.

profiles.summary: Matt Martians and Pyramid Vritra's production duo, from the Super D3Shay experiments through four Jet Age album cycles and their later solo extensions.
profiles.tagline: Odd Future's science-fiction production wing builds its own catalog.

chapters.title: The production branch begins before its final name
chapters.dek: Matt Martians' Super 3 concept and the Super D3Shay collaboration with brandUn DeShay formed the earliest version of the production world that became The Jet Age of Tomorrow.

chapters.title: Martians and Vritra launch the Jet Age
chapters.dek: The duo released Voyager and Journey to the 5th Echelon in rapid succession, building an instrumental and psychedelic counterworld beside Odd Future's vocal mixtapes.

chapters.title: JellyFish Mentality expands the guest network
chapters.dek: The 2013 album and bonus EP placed the duo's production inside a broader collaborator network, showing how the subgroup could connect Odd Future to voices outside it.

chapters.title: A final duo album turns into two solo continuations
chapters.dek: God's Poop or Clouds? is the current final Jet Age album. Martians later said he was content with that ending and understood his solo records as an extension of the same ideas; Vritra's large solo catalog supplies the other continuation.
